overview_markdown:
## Overview

thepopebot is a self-hosted personal AI agent platform that combines chat, a coding environment, and a communication layer into a single JavaScript app. Its core architecture is 'three doors, one brain': browser chat, Telegram (with per-user verification), and live code workspaces all route into a central event handler that picks the coding agent, manages sessions, and orchestrates Docker containers. It is deliberately LLM-agnostic (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and agent-agnostic (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Pi, Kimi).

The standout differentiator is the split between **live chat** (agent runs in-process or in a headless container, streaming to your screen) and **agent jobs** (background workers that run in fresh Docker containers, open PRs, auto-merge, and DM you on completion). This makes it closer to an autonomous junior developer than a chatbot. Everything runs on your own hardware with your own tokens, giving it a strong local-first privacy posture.

Compared to OpenClaw, thepopebot trades ecosystem breadth for simplicity and unification — one app instead of a skills registry and multi-channel mesh. Recent commits show active, careful maintenance (fixing stale config caches, flexible Telegram webhook configuration), with rapid patch releases through v1.2.82. However, Slack and Discord integrations are still 'coming soon,' and the community footprint outside GitHub is minimal.
